---
title: "Release archives and export-ignore"
---

# Release archives and `export-ignore`

A source archive gives a recipient a snapshot without the repository's history. `git archive` reads a committed tree, so uncommitted edits and untracked files are absent. Use `export-ignore` to omit tracked development material from an archive while retaining it in the repository.

## Build and inspect an archive

In a repository with a commit, run:

```sh
git archive --format=tar --prefix=desk-api/ HEAD > /tmp/desk-api.tar
tar -tf /tmp/desk-api.tar
```

The trailing slash in `--prefix` puts the files under a directory when extracted. `HEAD` selects the current commit; a tag or another commit can select a release. List the archive before distributing it and test a build from an extracted copy. The archive is not a clone: it has no Git history, branches, or `.git` directory. Git submodule entries are not recursively packaged as their contents.

Suppose `notes/` contains tracked maintainer notes that are unnecessary in the release. Add this to the root `.gitattributes`, then commit it:

```gitattributes
/notes export-ignore
```

Create the archive again from that commit. `notes/` remains tracked and visible in a clone, but is excluded from the archive. This differs from `.gitignore`, which affects untracked files considered for addition. Neither rule removes a secret already stored in Git; keep secrets out of commits and rotate exposed credentials.

By default archive attributes come from the tree being archived. An uncommitted edit to `.gitattributes` therefore does not change a normal `git archive HEAD`. `--worktree-attributes` uses working-tree attributes as well, useful for testing a packaging change before committing it. Local `$GIT_DIR/info/attributes` can also affect the result, so build and inspect releases in a controlled environment.

## Embed the release commit

Add this line to `.gitattributes`:

```gitattributes
VERSION export-subst
```

Create and commit `VERSION` with the literal contents below:

```text
Commit: $Format:%H$
```

When archiving a commit or tag, Git substitutes the commit ID in the archived `VERSION`; the tracked file itself remains unchanged. A raw tree ID does not provide the commit metadata needed for this substitution. Use this as traceability information, not as a signature or proof of provenance.

## Check yourself

1. Why does editing a tracked file without committing it not change an archive of `HEAD`?
2. Does `export-ignore` remove `notes/` from a clone or from past commits?
3. How can you verify that an archive has all files needed to build?

**Answers:** (1) The command reads the committed tree. (2) Neither; it controls Git archive output. (3) List it, extract it into a clean directory, and run the project's build and tests there.

See the [git archive manual](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-archive) and [archive attributes](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes#_creating_an_archive).
